source.title: Scalable and Interpretable Representation Alignment with Ordinal Similarity
source.authors: Diogo Soares; Pankhil Gawade; Andrea Dittadi; Ewa Szczurek

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures representation alignment with new ordinal metrics rather than the metrics used in prior convergence work, and reports results for training checkpoints, model scales, and cross-modal embeddings.
record.gate_note: Rows cover measured alignment across CLIP scales and distinct training seeds, and experiments where the authors vary the similarity metric, data perturbation, or distance proxy. The same-seed comparison to a model's own final representation is not an independent-model result. Figure 6 approximation-error comparisons are left out because they assess estimation accuracy, not representation alignment. Results cited from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests V6 through metric disagreements, sample and dimensionality sweeps, outlier perturbations, and distance-proxy comparisons. Its CLIP encoders are jointly optimized for cross-modal alignment, so their alignment does not establish spontaneous convergence between independently trained models. Ordinal agreement across seeds does not directly measure shared features or subspaces.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors present TSI/QSI as interpretable, robust, scalable alignment measures with provable computational and approximation properties, validated on ViT training and CLIP alignment. They report metric failure modes and attribute the CLIP CKA decline to dimensionality sensitivity. These demonstrations do not establish universal convergence or its causes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ordinal triplet and quadruplet agreement (TSI/QSI), rather than reproducing the original studies' alignment measurements. It also compares against CKA and neighborhood metrics.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with similarity metric, sample count, dimensionality, neighborhood size, distance proxy (negative dot product versus Euclidean), perturbation strength, and embedding dimensionality across CLIP scales. TSI/QSI trends across CLIP scales are reported for both Euclidean and negative cosine similarity.

fits_no_version.finding: Distinct-seed ViTs develop similar but non-identical ordinal distance relationships during training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks trained from different initializations develop similar relational geometry, without establishing shared features/subspaces or substantial residual disagreement.

fits_no_version.finding: TSI/QSI image-to-label-prompt alignment increases across three jointly trained CLIP variants under both tested distance choices.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Higher-performing CLIP variants exhibit greater ordinal cross-modal alignment on ImageNet label prompts when cross-modal alignment is explicitly optimized.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306 (2026)
record.problems: The CLIP and training-convergence results are presented in figures without individual numerical alignment scores in the text. The cross-modal experiment uses prompt-based label embeddings rather than captions. The distinct-seed result is described as similar but not identical, without a numerical degree of incompleteness. Error bars or other uncertainty estimates are not stated for these alignment results.
record.rows_left_out: Section 6.3, Figure 6: approximation-error comparisons were left out because they measure estimator accuracy rather than representation alignment. Section 6.4, Figure 7: the same-seed trajectory is omitted because it compares checkpoints with their own model's final representation rather than independently trained models. Other purely theoretical properties and cited findings are not cataloged as empirical alignment rows.

untested.parts: No scale-dependent comparison between independently trained models with differing architectures, objectives, and data. CLIP's within-model cross-modal alignment is explicitly trained.
No spontaneous cross-modal convergence between independently trained vision and language models on image-caption pairs; CLIP alignment is an optimization target, and evaluation uses label prompts.
No direct identification of shared features or subspaces across seeds, or comparison of individual units and bases. Ordinal geometric agreement is a related measurement.
No representation mapping, stitching, transfer-loss measurement, or unpaired interchangeability experiment.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
No out-of-distribution evaluation, systematic semantic input-distribution comparison, or empirical sweep across neighborhood sizes.
No quantified substantial incompleteness, established plateau, or causal test of shared training data/objectives versus a common model of reality.

missing.what: Comparator outcomes completing the constructed metric-disagreement examples: local permutation gives MutualNN=1 and CKA→1; cluster translation gives MutualNN=CKNNA=1, while ordinal scores fall below 1.
CKNNA and MutualNN also capture increasing CLIP alignment across scales. These reported comparator trends complete the contrast with declining CKA.

record.verdict_notes: Only the supplied text was used; plotted coordinates were unavailable. Monotonic trends and qualitative outcomes are supported by explicit prose, but individual alignment scores and uncertainty cannot be recovered. The illustrative 0.57 score in Section 6.5 is not identified as a particular model's measured result.

versions.untested_parts: The CLIP scale experiment tests three variants from one model family and does not vary training objective or data. It does not establish convergence across independently trained models with broadly different architectures, objectives, and datasets.
Uses images paired with prompt-based label embeddings, not image-caption pairs. The tested models are CLIP variants; the text does not establish that both modalities independently improve.
The seed comparison measures ordinal distance alignment, not shared features, shared subspaces, or individual units.
No mapping between model representations, layer stitching, relative-representation transfer, or alignment without paired data is tested.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are examined.
The experiments vary metric, sample count, dimensionality, outlier strength, and distance proxy. They do not test out-of-distribution inputs or every reasonable similarity measure.

The distinct-seed result indicates alignment is not identical, but does not establish a plateau, quantify how far from complete alignment it is, or determine whether shared data/objectives explain the alignment.
